items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: how I come to get into the George Lewis band, I played with Eddie Morris back at Linfans, back on Canal Boulevard.

ctx.x: And we had a crippled fellow on the clarinet. I can't think of his name now. He's dead. And sometimes we have George Lewis and drag. Well, the piano player, I didn't know his name. Then we had another fellow by the name of Alfred used to play sax with us sometime when we couldn't get clarinet. Well, how I come to get into the George Lewis band, I played with Eddie Morris back at Linfans, back on Canal Boulevard. One Sunday afternoon. And George had a job at the corner from Drag's house. And he needed a drummer.…
Well, somebody told me a few months ago, Reverend Kershaw was a professor. Did you ever hear any of them?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: Eddie Morris needed a drummer... Took four of us to jail anyhow... I forget who we had on piano.

ctx.x: So we started playing down in the little country parishes. And every Sunday during the summer they had picnics down there where we'd go and they'd hire us to play the picnics. Yeah. It was mostly colored picnics and everything else. So one night, you know one Sunday afternoon, Eddie Morris needed a drummer. He was playing out here on Canal Boulevard at Linford's.
